# Second Year Fantasy Basketball Breakouts

Locked On Fantasy Basketball, 2026-09-04, 29:00. https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo

## Summary

Josh Lloyd looks at how NBA players develop from their rookie year to their second year, using six seasons of data (2020-21 to 2025-26), and then goes through this season's sophomore class. Second-year players are much more fantasy relevant than rookies. About 60% of rookies improve and 41% climb at least 50 ranking spots. ADP is good at picking out the second-year players who get drafted early. Late-round sophomore flyers rarely work out: only 13% of those drafted in the 101 to 150 range finished top 100. He sees Cooper Flagg as a safe late first-round pick but thinks his $60 auction price is too high. He sees Kon Knueppel, VJ Edgecombe and Dylan Harper as overdrafted. His main breakout targets are Derik Queen and Collin Murray-Boyles, with Cedric Coward as a possible third. Jeremiah Fears, Egor Demin and Joan Beringer are late flyers, and Ace Bailey is overdrafted.

## Rules and methods

- [2:24](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=144) Second-year players are much more fantasy relevant than rookies. Over six years, top 50 category players went from 3 as rookies to 8 in year two, top 100 from 11 to 31, and top 150 from 20 to 54.
  > "We had three players as rookies be top 50 guys for category leagues."
- [4:50](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=290) Across all rookies, 60% improved in year two, and 41% improved by at least 50 ranking slots.
  > "41% of all rookies improve by at least 50 ranking slots in year two."
- [5:36](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=336) Rookie rank and sophomore rank have a correlation of about 0.61. Most players who are relevant in year two were already somewhat relevant in year one. Only 30 players in six years jumped from outside the top 150 to inside it.
  > "Only 30 of those players over that six year period were not top 150 relevant as rookies"
- [6:32](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=392) ADP is good with second-year players at the top end. All seven with a top 50 ADP finished top 100. Of those with an ADP of 51 to 100, 72% finished top 100.
  > "Only 72% of those finish in the top 100 and 94% of those finish in the top 150."
- [7:03](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=423) Second-year flyers with an ADP of 101 to 150 hit only 13% of the time for top 100 and 33% for top 150. Undrafted sophomores almost never become relevant.
  > "So a 13% hit rate on secondyear flyers. 33% of them did end up as top 150 players."
- [7:59](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=479) Late flyers usually do not work out. That is accepted as part of the cost of drafting in that area.
  > "We know that when we're drafting them late that that's that's part of the cost of doing business"
- [13:00](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=780) In auctions, people tend to overpay for top-end players and underpay for players in the middle range.
  > "I think that in general people do overpric topend players and underpric the middle range like a lot."
- [14:04](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=844) If a pick finishes a few spots below where you took it, that barely matters. A big miss, like 11th to 30th, does matter.
  > "But a four or five spot difference, which is probably half a fantasy point or, you know, 0.1 steals, doesn't matter."
- [21:44](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=1304) Be wary of unsustainable shooting splits, such as very high percentages on twos and threes. They tend to regress.
  > "Bro's hitting 75 on his twos. He's at 50 on his threes. That's just not going to happen, is it?"
- [22:26](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=1346) Steals and free throw percentage are the two categories that vary most from year to year.
  > "Free throw percentage in steals the two most variable year on year."
- [27:28](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=1648) Backup bigs who would become must-rosters if the starter misses games are worth drafting in games cap, limited transaction, roto and weekly lock formats. They are harder to justify in daily leagues where you use your bench all the time.
  > "So in games cap formats, in limited transaction formats, in roto leagues, in weekly lock leagues, he has to be drafted"
